title: A Wrinkle in Time
synopsis: Your dad disappeared into space-time. Three strange Mrs Ws are at the door. The tesseract is, apparently, a verb. Go find him.

nodes.text: Mrs Whatsit is at the door in a thunderstorm. She mentions a tesseract. You realize you are, technically, in a novel. The road still runs toward Charles Wallace. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Listen” and choosing “Stay polite.”

choices.consequence: You choose to listen. By Charles Wallace, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to stay polite. By Charles Wallace, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Your tiny brother Charles Wallace, somehow, has been corresponding with all three Mrs Ws by name. Calvin comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Trust him” and “Question him.” By Calvin, the people waiting will remember which instinct carried you forward.

choices.consequence: You commit to trust him. It carries you toward Calvin, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You commit to question him. It carries you toward Calvin, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: A schoolmate named Calvin shows up because, the Mrs Ws say, he's part of it. He is, surprisingly, nice. Mrs Who's Quote will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Welcome him” than after “Be suspicious.”

choices.consequence: You welcome him. The path to Mrs Who's Quote opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You commit to be suspicious. It carries you toward Mrs Who's Quote, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Mrs Who speaks only in quotations. The quotations are, in places, useful. Both choices lead to First Tesseract, but “Note them” arrives there with a different cost than “Just listen.” In Mrs Who's Quote, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You choose to note them. By First Tesseract, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You just listen. The path to First Tesseract opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You tesseract. The sensation is unpleasant. You arrive on a planet with too many flowers. The road still runs toward Uriel. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Smell a flower” and choosing “Don't touch anything.”

choices.consequence: You smell a flower. The path to Uriel opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You commit to don't touch anything. It carries you toward Uriel, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Uriel is, apparently, the good place. You meet a centaur who explains evil as a darkness across the universe. Camazotz Glimpse is already waiting. What changes is whether “Look at the darkness” or “Don't look” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You choose to look at the darkness. By Camazotz Glimpse, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to don't look. By Camazotz Glimpse, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: You glimpse Camazotz, the dark planet. Your dad is on it. The darkness, you realize, eats things slowly. Mrs Whatsit's Form is already waiting. What changes is whether “Vow to go” or “Demand a plan first” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You vow to go. The path to Mrs Whatsit's Form opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You demand a plan first. The path to Mrs Whatsit's Form opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Mrs Whatsit transforms into a creature with wings. Charles Wallace, on her back, is, you realize, exactly his happiest. Both choices lead to Happy Medium, but “Ride her” arrives there with a different cost than “Walk.”

choices.consequence: You ride her. The path to Happy Medium opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You walk. The path to Happy Medium opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: The Happy Medium has, in his cave, a crystal ball that shows your father. He is alive. He is also a long way away. Camazotz Approach will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Believe it” than after “Verify it.”

choices.consequence: You commit to believe it. It carries you toward Camazotz Approach, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You verify it. The path to Camazotz Approach opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You and Charles Wallace and Calvin approach Camazotz. The planet looks, ominously, like a suburb. Both choices lead to Identical Children, but “Walk in” arrives there with a different cost than “Sneak in.” At Identical Children, the decision will matter as memory as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You choose to walk in. By Identical Children, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You commit to sneak in. It carries you toward Identical Children, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Children bouncing identical balls in identical rhythms. Charles Wallace, you realize, is in danger of being absorbed. Central Intelligence is already waiting. What changes is whether “Hold his hand tight” or “Distract him” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You choose to hold his hand tight. By Central Intelligence, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You distract him. The path to Central Intelligence opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: The CENTRAL Intelligence building is, on the map, the center of evil. You go in. You cannot avoid Charles Wallace, Taken; you can only decide whether “Take the front door” or “Find another way” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You take the front door. The path to Charles Wallace, Taken opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You choose to find another way. By Charles Wallace, Taken, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Charles Wallace is taken by IT. He talks in a flat voice. He is, technically, still your brother. Your Father comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Fight to bring him back” and “Negotiate with IT.”

choices.consequence: You fight to bring him back. The path to Your Father opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You commit to negotiate with IT. It carries you toward Your Father, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: You find your father in a clear column. He is older, gaunter, alive. He doesn't, for a second, recognize you. The Way Out comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Speak his name” and “Hug him.”

choices.consequence: You speak his name. The path to The Way Out opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You hug him. The path to The Way Out opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: The way out, as ever, is the way you came in. The way out is also, this time, harder. Mrs Which's Voice is already waiting. What changes is whether “Carry Charles Wallace” or “Coax him out” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You choose to carry Charles Wallace. By Mrs Which's Voice, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You commit to coax him out. It carries you toward Mrs Which's Voice, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Mrs Which, the oldest of the three, finally speaks. Her voice is slow and heavy. The advice, by now, is one word: love. Both choices lead to Charles Wallace, Returning, but “Use love” arrives there with a different cost than “Use love and a plan.”

choices.consequence: You use love. The path to Charles Wallace, Returning opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You use love and a plan. The path to Charles Wallace, Returning opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Your love, plainly and embarrassingly out loud, reaches him. He blinks. The flatness retreats. Both choices lead to The Run, but “Hold him” arrives there with a different cost than “Get him moving.” By The Run, the people waiting will remember which instinct carried you forward.

choices.consequence: You choose to hold him. By The Run, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You get him moving. The path to The Run opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You run. The corridors of CENTRAL fold and unfold. The Mrs Ws are, in the corner of your eye, helping. The road still runs toward Back on Uriel. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Trust them” and choosing “Trust your feet.”

choices.consequence: You commit to trust them. It carries you toward Back on Uriel, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You trust your feet. The path to Back on Uriel opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You arrive back on Uriel briefly. The Mrs Ws thank you. Charles Wallace, weirdly, asks for a sandwich. You cannot avoid Home; you can only decide whether “Make the sandwich” or “Promise one at home” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You choose to make the sandwich. By Home, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to promise one at home. By Home, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: You land in your front yard. Mom comes out screaming. Dad is, this time, in the picture in a way he hasn't been in years. Both choices lead to School, Monday, but “Hug everyone” arrives there with a different cost than “Sit on the porch and breathe.”

choices.consequence: You commit to hug everyone. It carries you toward School, Monday, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Sit on the porch and breathe
choices.consequence: You commit to sit on the porch and breathe. It carries you toward School, Monday, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: You go back to school Monday. People don't believe what you tell them. You decide what you'll tell them now. The distance between Quietly Strange and The Book begins with the choice between “Tell the truth” and “Stay quiet.” A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Family, Finally in play.

choices.consequence: You commit to tell the truth. It carries you toward Quietly Strange, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You choose to stay quiet. By The Book, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You take the third path. The path to Family, Finally opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You become, in your school, the slightly strange kid. Calvin, mercifully, becomes the slightly strange kid too. You are, at fourteen, a small good resistance to whatever darkness is closest. The road into Quietly Strange began with “Tell the truth” in School, Monday; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You write, decades later, a book about it. The book is, in fact, the one you read as a kid. The cycle closes. The road into The Book began with “Stay quiet” in School, Monday; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

Your dad stays. Charles Wallace, less weird than he was, grows up. Calvin marries you, in a long-running joke that becomes a real thing. The Mrs Ws send Christmas cards. Mrs Who's are in three languages.
